result.text: After nine months, mean spleen volume decreased 29% in the 30 Units/kg group and 40% in the 60 Units/kg group. In a gender subgroup analysis of percentage change from baseline in spleen volume, the within-subgroup one-sample t-test p-values were significant in both female (p=0.0001 and p<0.0001) and male (p=0.0004 and p<0.0001) patients.

indication.text: Long-term enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) for adults with a confirmed diagnosis of Type 1 Gaucher disease.

citations.quote: ELELYSO™ (taliglucerase alfa) for injection is a hydrolytic lysosomal glucocerebroside-specific enzyme indicated for long-term enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) for adults with a confirmed diagnosis of Type 1 Gaucher disease.

target_moa.text: Taliglucerase alfa is a hydrolytic lysosomal glucocerebroside-specific enzyme (recombinant human glucocerebrosidase) that compensates for the enzymatic deficiency underlying Gaucher disease, reducing accumulation of glucocerebroside within macrophages.

citations.quote: Elelyso (taliglucerase alfa), is a hydrolytic lysosomal glucocerebroside-specific enzyme expressed in genetically modified carrot plant root cells in a disposable bioreactor system.
Gaucher disease results in a deficiency of the lysosomal enzyme glucocerebrosidase (GCB) and causes an accumulation of glucocerebroside within macrophages (Gaucher cells).
Enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) designed to compensate for the underlying enzymatic defect has been the cornerstone of treatment for Gaucher disease.

modality.text: Enzyme (recombinant human glucocerebrosidase expressed in carrot plant root cells).

citations.quote: Elelyso (taliglucerase alfa), is a hydrolytic lysosomal glucocerebroside-specific enzyme expressed in genetically modified carrot plant root cells in a disposable bioreactor system.

key_safety.text: Infusion reactions (including allergic reactions) within 24 hours were the most common reactions (44%-46% of patients); anaphylaxis occurred in 9% (3/32) of treatment-naïve patients in PB-06-001. Other commonly observed adverse reactions (≥10% of patients) included URTI/nasopharyngitis (22%/18%), pharyngitis/throat infection (19%/4%), headache (19%/11%), and arthralgia (13%/11%).

citations.quote: Infusion reactions (including allergic reactions), defined as a reaction occurring within 24 hours of the infusion, were the most commonly observed reactions in patients (44%-46%) treated with ELELYSO in clinical studies
